dimensions.risk: low: the code half (scanner lift, lint wiring, block rewrite) is proven by mutation and every guard is green; the only defect that matters is one false sentence in the prime, which is prose no lane reads and which a shell author would act on

verdict: Accept with small remediation. The scan, the lift, and the block fix are correct and pinned: all four guards exit 0 in my clone (74 fences, 33 shipped shell files, 95 tracked shell files, 19+7 fixture, audit-lockins), contract-regressions.sh exits 0, mutations M1/M2/M3 fail with the exact FAIL lines the record quotes, and the lifted function body is byte-identical (39 lines). The one finding that survives at 'important' is in the deliverable the request was mostly about: the prime's new section says 'Below the pipe buffer the writer finishes before the reader leaves, so the check passes for years'. That sentence is in neither archived record and my measurement shows it is false for the section's own example writer: `tar tzf | grep -q` misfires 20 of 50 at a 4.8 KB listing and 50 of 50 at 14 KB, both far under the 64 KiB pipe buffer; REQ-593's own record and my pinned-CPU replay (1 of 500) show 36 KB was never silent. The 0-of-50 / 50-of-50 figures are real but belong to one writer (bash builtin printf emitting a single string). Fix: attribute the numbers to their writer and delete the mechanism sentence. Everything else is low: a stale 'fourteen ... fixture below' comment line the lift left behind, a hand-back citation of a work.md substep that does not exist, a record sentence that places a prose list item 'in a fence', and a two-line probe under prose that says 'first hit wins'. Two pre-existing issues outside the write set (audit mktemp fall-through, 4-space fence not opened) are discovered tasks, not regressions.

confirmed_findings.title: Prime line 53 teaches a false safe zone below the pipe buffer; the section's own example writer (tar tzf) is wrong 20 of 50 at 4.8 KB
confirmed_findings.detail: New section, _dev/primes/prime-shell-commands.md line 53: 'REQ-593 measured 0 false verdicts in 50 runs at 36 KB of producer output and 50 of 50 at 200 KB. Below the pipe buffer the writer finishes before the reader leaves, so the check passes for years; above it the check is wrong every time.' The numbers are in REQ-593's archive (lines 310-311, 424-425) but were measured for one writer, bash's builtin printf emitting one 36 KB string. The same archive (lines 108, 169-170) says that exact output misfired 2-3 in 500 on a pinned CPU, which is the failure that opened REQ-593, so 36 KB was never the silent side. The mechanism sentence ('writer finishes before the reader leaves') appears in neither REQ-593 nor REQ-594 (grep 'pipe buffer' over both archives: only REQ-593:106, a different claim). It is false for any writer that flushes in chunks: the size that flips depends on how the writer flushes, not on the pipe buffer. The request's own wording ('silent below roughly 36 KB') carried the same generalization, so the builder followed it, but the request asked for the measured window and the builder added an unmeasured mechanism. A shell author reading this section learns that sub-buffer producers are safe; the record's Implementation Summary uses exactly that reasoning ('far below the window') for the ollama block. The next sentence ('A producer that prints a hundred bytes today carries the same shape and flips the day it grows') is the correct guidance and the window sentence undercuts it. Reviewers 1 and 3 found this; reviewer 2 marked the window as 'held' from the archive lines alone without measuring. I ran the experiment and took reviewers 1 and 3.

confirmed_findings.suggested_fix: Replace the two sentences with something like: 'Timing decides, not content. REQ-593 measured bash's builtin printf writing one string: 0 of 50 at 36 KB on an idle host, 2-3 of 500 at the same 36 KB on a pinned CPU (the incident that opened the request), 50 of 50 at 200 KB. The size that flips depends on how the writer flushes, not on the pipe buffer: tar tzf misfires 20 of 50 at a 5 KB listing. There is no safe size.' Keep 'A producer that prints a hundred bytes today carries the same shape and flips the day it grows.' Also soften the record's 'far below the window' for the ollama block to 'small, and not a live failure today' so the record does not rely on the deleted claim.

confirmed_findings.title: Under the prose 'first hit wins', the new setup line ollama_models=... is a line that always exits 0
confirmed_findings.detail: skills/do-work-knowledge/actions/memory-reference.md line 88. The prose above says 'Probe for an embedding backend; first hit wins.' The old block was three one-line probes. The new first line is setup, not a probe: evaluated as its own line with no ollama installed it exits 0, so a reader treating each line as a probe meets a hit before any backend is checked. The comment marks it as setup and running the four lines as one script gives the right answer (exit 1/1/0 across no-ollama, failing stub, embed stub), so this is a shape mismatch with the introducing sentence, not a wrong result. A one-line form `grep -qiE 'embed' <<<"$(ollama list 2>/dev/null || true)"` keeps the three-probe shape, keeps the prime's capture-then-herestring form, and passes the shared scanner. Found by reviewer 3; reproduced. Reviewers 1 and 2 did not raise it; I keep it at low because the block behaves correctly when run as written.

disagreements_and_how_settled: The window sentence in the prime (line 53). Reviewer 2 listed 'Prime's cited window 0 of 50 at 36 KB, 50 of 50 at 200 KB (held: REQ-593 archive lines 251 and 310-311)' as a met claim and scored 93; reviewers 1 (important, score 78) and 3 (medium, score 84) said the added mechanism sentence is false. Reviewer 2 only checked that the numbers appear in the archive; it did not check the sentence 'Below the pipe buffer the writer finishes before the reader leaves' against the archive or against a measurement. I ran the experiment: tar tzf (the section's own example writer) misfires 20/50 at 4.8 KB and 50/50 at 14 KB, an echo loop 2/50 at ~6 KB, all under the 64 KiB buffer; the numbers hold only for bash's builtin printf writing one string. I took reviewers 1 and 3 and rated it important, because the prime is the deliverable the request was mainly about and the sentence teaches the opposite of the section's purpose. Reviewer 1's stronger framing ('36 KB was never the silent side') is also supported: the archive reports 2-3/500 pinned and I measured 1/500 pinned.

Severity of the 'byte-for-byte' comment claim. Reviewer 2 and 3 both flag the stale line 18; reviewer 3 additionally notes the hand-back (not the record) is where the 'and its contract comment' wording lives. Both agree on substance; I verified the body is identical and the comment differs at line 35 and is stale at line 18. Kept as one low finding.

The 'first hit wins' two-line probe (reviewer 3 only). Reviewers 1 and 2 did not raise it. I reproduced the per-line exit codes (line 88 exits 0 alone) and the correct whole-block result (1/1/0), and verified the one-line alternative is scanner-clean. Kept at low: it is a shape mismatch with the introducing prose, not a wrong verdict.

Whether the pre-existing audit mktemp fall-through and the 4-space fence gap count against REQ-600. Reviewer 2 raised both and marked both pre-existing; I confirmed lines 14-18 of the audit are identical at the parent and the fence regex is unchanged and disclosed in the hand-back.
